findings: Our rain chances were tested on about 179 past days that were kept aside while the model was built (March to September 2026), at the Perth Metro gauge. Judged on whether it rained or not, they scored about 40 to 43% better than simply using the usual chance of rain for that time of year.
For how much rain falls, our forecasts did about as well as the weather models themselves: 126 of 126 side-by-side comparisons with them were too close to call.

So the rain chances are the most useful part of this forecast for the next two or three days. Further out, the forecast shows how many of five international weather models expect rain. That is a guide, not a probability.
Rain is measured at the Bureau's Perth Metro gauge in Mount Lawley, from 9am to 9am. Showers are patchy, so your suburb can get more or less.
how_to_read: Chance of any rain: the chance of at least 0.2 mm at the gauge, from our calibrated forecast. It is shown only for the days we can forecast this way.

Possible rainfall: a 50% chance of at least the first number and a 25% chance of at least the second, as the Bureau uses it. On days marked as model guidance, it is the range of the five models' totals instead.
Each day's rain covers 9am that day to 9am the next.
Temperatures and winds are the middle value of the five weather models.
